gloss: tsukudani; small foods simmered in soy sauce and mirin

definitions.gloss: tsukudani, food simmered in soy sauce and mirin
definitions.explanation: A Japanese preserved food made by simmering ingredients in soy sauce, mirin, and sugar until the liquid is absorbed. Strongly flavored, eaten in small amounts with rice.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昆布|こんぶ}→昆布：04934_konbu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{佃煮|つくだに}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{ご飯|はん}→ご飯：00776_gohan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{合|あ}います→合う：10466_au⟧。
examples.english: Kelp tsukudani goes well with rice.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{小魚|こざかな}→小魚：28694_kozakana⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{佃煮|つくだに}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}りました→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother made tsukudani with small fish.

examples.japanese: {佃煮|つくだに}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{保存|ほぞん}→保存：03626_hozon⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{効|き}く→効く：01932_kiku⟧⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧⟦{便利|べんり}→便利：00830_benri⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: Tsukudani is convenient because it keeps well.

notes:
{佃煮|つくだに} is named after ⟦{佃島|つくだじま}→佃島：noentry⟧, an area in Tokyo where this cooking method originated.

Common ingredients:
- ⟦{昆布|こんぶ}→昆布：04934_konbu⟧ (kelp)
- ⟦{小魚|こざかな}→小魚：28694_kozakana⟧ (small fish like whitebait)
- ⟦{海苔|のり}→海苔：10391_nori⟧ (seaweed)
- ⟦{貝|かい}→貝：02145_kai⟧ (shellfish)
- ⟦{山椒|さんしょう}→山椒：12412_sanshou⟧ (Japanese pepper)

Characteristics:
- Dark, glossy appearance from soy sauce
- Sweet-savory-salty flavor
- Intensely flavored - eaten in small portions
- Long shelf life due to high salt/sugar content

Serving: Typically eaten as a condiment with plain rice, in ⟦{お茶漬|ちゃづ}け→茶漬け：04987_chazuke⟧, or in ⟦{お弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧.
